result.title: Byte Patches versus BPE at Matched Data: A Matched-Twin Comparison at 350M Parameters
result.comment: 18 pages, 3 figures. Code, checkpoints and evaluation suites: https://github.com/AsadullahMaliyawala/bytelm-local64
result.summary: We compare a MEGABYTE-style byte-patch Transformer with a 64-byte sliding local decoder (local64) to a matched byte-level 8k BPE decoder (BPE-8k) under identical raw bytes, document order, and approximately matched bytes per optimizer step: 350M parameters and 10 billion training bytes. Under matched-span document sliding (identical scored byte ranges), BPE-8k leads with relative gaps of -5.2%, -4.9%, -9.3% and -6.1% in bits per byte (overall, text, code, math; paired bootstrap). Downstream, CharBench equal fine-tuning favors local64 (53.7% vs 40.0%), fact200 favors BPE-8k (16.5% vs 7.0%), and PIQA (raw and length-normalized) and ARC-Easy length-normalized favor BPE-8k after Holm correction at alpha = 0.05; remaining tasks are ties. Evaluation pitfalls that changed conclusions include context-length extrapolation past the BPE training context, bits per token reported as bits per byte, and inconsistent byte denominators. Unlike controlled tokenizer studies that vary the subword tokenizer under a fixed token budget, or FLOP-controlled byte-model scaling studies, we hold the raw bytes, their order and the optimizer recipe fixed and ask whether a fixed-patch byte model can replace the tokenizer at all. Limits: one size, one seed, one 8k vocabulary fixed before the runs, and a known difference in embedding initialization between the twins.

AI.brief_summary: 在相同原始字节、文档顺序和近似相同的每步字节预算下，比较 350M 参数的 MEGABYTE 式字节 patch Transformer（64 字节滑动局部解码器）与 8k BPE 解码器，并报告 bpb 差异、下游任务结果及影响结论的评测陷阱。
AI.relevance_reason: 其固定 patch 表示与匹配数据孪生对照、以及「bits per token 误报为 bits per byte」、上下文外推等评测陷阱，可供核查视觉 patch 粒度与 latent 表示比较的公平性，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理或推理期 latent 状态。
